text.text:
I’ve always associated EL&N with impeccable aesthetics and the polished visual experience they showcase on Instagram. That’s why walking into this branch today was genuinely shocking the space looks nothing like the standard the brand claims to represent.

The ambience, which is supposed to be EL&N’s strongest point, was visibly deteriorated. The sofas were torn, peeling and with the foam fully exposed, looking more like discarded furniture than seating in a premium café. The chairs were in the same condition dirty, cracked and falling apart. None of this reflects the “instagrammable” identity the brand markets so heavily.

The floor was dirty, stained and clearly not cleaned recently. The counter displaying the cakes had dark marks, accumulated grime and exposed cardboard boxes, completely breaking the illusion of care. Even worse, there was a regular bin placed right next to the food, with the orange bin liner fully visible highly unappealing and questionable from a hygiene perspective.

The ceiling had holes, loose panels, cracked paint and exposed structures, giving the entire space an abandoned feel. The service area behind the counter looked disorganised, with stained shelves and utensils on display. The bathroom had an unpleasant smell, reinforcing the sense of poor maintenance.

Nothing about this visit reflected the visual identity EL&N is known for. The environment was so uncomfortable that I couldn’t bring myself to eat. It felt like a place without management, without maintenance and entirely inconsistent with the brand’s promise.

I sincerely hope this branch receives immediate attention, because the aesthetics the very thing that makes EL&N what it is were simply not present today.

I came here after visiting the exquisite brunch in Covent Garden.
But unlike that one this is a completely different experience. First of all, I noticed immediately that the place is rundown (see picture). But most importantly the food is very far from the other branch when it comes to quality. It was not particularly warm and I think the portion was very small for the price (15.99£) and when I brought it up they just told me that that was the veggie breakfast. In the - tablet and self ordering - menu only the normal one was available because apparently they didn't have some ingredients, however we sorted it out. And then they brought me a portion that looks much less than the one in the picture which is false advertising. (I forgot to take a picture at the beginning of the meal but in this one I had barely just started and had none of the beans which are half a portion compared to their picture menu). The toilets also could have been better cared for. For hand shop there is a cheap plastic dispenser that has curdled up and had some white things floating on top.
Their matcha latte (the only reason my rating is 3 and not 2 stars) - while tasty - it's quite sweet which makes me think they cater more to a young audience with Instagramable drinks rather to actual quality. Or they have just put more of an effort right now into their newest Covent Garden brunch.
I'm Soho there are much better options for breakfast and for value for money.

text.text:
If you’re hunting for a cosy English breakfast spot in Soho, KOZZEE is one of those places that instantly catches your eye with its warm lighting and chilled, rustic vibe. It feels like a proper little hideout in the middle of the city — perfect for a relaxed brunch or a quick breakfast stop.

The menu is solid, offering everything from a classic full English to pancakes, French toast, and avocado-based dishes. The coffee is definitely a highlight — smooth, well-made, and exactly what you’d expect from a central London brunch café. Some dishes, especially the French toast and breakfast plates, are genuinely enjoyable and well-presented.

Service can be a bit hit or miss. While many staff are friendly and attentive, the experience isn’t always consistent. On a good day, it feels welcoming and efficient, but at busy times it can feel slightly rushed.

In terms of pricing, it’s very much “Soho standard” — on the higher side for what you get. Some people feel the portions and quality don’t always justify the cost, especially when dishes arrive less hot than expected or seating feels cramped.

Overall, KOZZEE is a decent brunch spot with a great vibe and good coffee, but it’s not without its flaws. If you’re nearby and want a cosy breakfast experience, it’s worth a try — just go in with realistic expectations.

Overall, a fun, energetic place and a solid choice for breakfast or brunch in Soho.

The place has that cozy, slightly quirky London café vibe—busy, a bit packed, but full of energy. You can tell it’s a popular spot, and for good reason. The atmosphere is lively and welcoming, perfect to kickstart your day in Soho.

I tried the avocado salmon along with eggs Benedict, and both were absolutely spot on. The eggs were perfectly poached with that rich, runny yolk, and the flavors were well balanced. The salmon and avocado combo felt fresh and satisfying, while the hollandaise sauce on the Benedict added that indulgent touch without being too heavy.

Paired it with a really good cup of coffee, which complemented the meal perfectly—smooth, rich, and exactly what you want with a proper breakfast.

Overall, great food, generous portions, and a vibe that makes you want to sit a little longer (even though it’s quite busy). Definitely one of those must-visit breakfast spots in London.

An Expensive, Disorganised Soho Disappointment

We tried for a table at Scarlett Green but couldn't get in, so we ended up at Toi & Moi on Berwick Street. It was a mistake. We spent £75.68, and the whole thing felt like a rip-off. They don't take AMEX.

**The Service**
There wasn't any. We had to go to the counter to place our order, and they made us pay upfront. On top of that, there was an £8.41 service charge on the bill. It makes no sense to charge for service you don't actually provide. My wife had to ask twice before she finally got her latte. No sauces were offered, and the whole experience was cold. You’re left wondering if we were treated this way because we’re Chinese; the service felt very off.

**The Food**
It was poor.

Sunrise French Toast: You can see it in image, there were no lemons to go with the smoked salmon, which it really needed.

Halal Breakfast: They served 1.5 sausages—cut in half to cook faster, I assume—and they were dry. The turkey bacon was dry, too. They only gave us one small portion of butter for the toast.

Egg Benedict: For the price, it was basic.

Don't bother with this place. It’s overpriced, the food is subpar, and the service is non-existent.

When I learned that there was a coffee shop just off the beaten path in Soho that just so happens to share the name with my absolute favorite coffee drink I had to check it out.

I arrived 10min before close, so, I wasn't able to really sit in the ambiance that is Flat White. That being said, the staff was friendly, and the service was quick.

Before I talk about the drink experience, some additional details... I fell in love with flat whites when I visited Australia several years ago and I've been ordering and making them at home ever since. One thing worth noting is that a UK (and much of Europe) flat white is not quite the same as an Aussie or American flat white. It's still the same components; rich and bold espresso shot(s) accompanied by textured milk (steam milk infused with air to create a velvety texture), but in the UK they are restricted to cup sizes for some reason (mostly to do with the ratio of espresso to cup size). I was presented with a 4oz to-go coffee cup. The flavor was great, and with execution solid.

While this particular drink was delicious, I think I still prefer an Aussie flat white (or American). Having the barely bigger than espresso size feels like the drink is condensed while I want to enjoy the drink and flavor for longer.

If you're someone who prefers things on the lighter or less sweet side, the dessert might be overwhelming, and I'd definitely recommend sharing a slice between two people rather than getting your own. Staff weren't unfriendly, just a bit slow/inattentive at times, so a little more attentiveness would've made the experience better.

That said, if you're a genuine chocolate lover, this is basically dessert heaven and worth the visit just for the presentation alone. The café had a cozy, old-world feel to it, and overall it was a nice stop for anyone with a serious sweet tooth — just don't expect top-notch service to match the desserts.

Amazing if you love chocolate, slightly too rich if you don't, and service could use some improvement.

But overall, it was essentially exactly what we were in the mood for. A Quiet spot with scones and tea. Not expensive, not fancy. Just right.

The barista was kind and warm, and it seems like a nice local spot with regulars.

I'd pop in for a scone and tea, if you're in the neighbourhood.

Made a comeback to this café after two whole years! It’s such a famous spot that during my last visit, even though there wasn’t a queue, the terrace was completely packed, so I had to take my order to a nearby park. I still vividly remember how beautifully they packaged everything back then, which left such a wonderful impression that I just had to return!

This time, I visited on a Saturday afternoon. The staff took our order downstairs (you pay on your way out!), and we were guided to the upper floor, where we managed to snag a table. The table turnover is surprisingly quick, so people come and go pretty fast. We ordered an English Breakfast tea, scones, and a strawberry cheesecake. The scones were, as expected, absolutely legendary! Having a proper cream tea after such a long time was pure bliss. Another huge plus is that if you need more hot water or milk for your tea, you can just ask the staff, and they’ll top it up right away—we actually asked for a milk refill once. The secret to a perfect scone is the harmony between the clotted cream and strawberry jam, and their clotted cream is incredibly rich and delicious.

But the real hidden gem of the day was the almond croissant we ordered on a whim. Apparently, it’s a low-key favorite here! It was quite big, and the nutty flavor of the almonds paired perfectly with the flaky, crispy pastry. Next time I come back, ordering the scone and the almond croissant together is a non-negotiable. Plus, the atmosphere is so cozy and it’s a fantastic place for a proper catch-up. Such a satisfying visit! ☕️🧁✨

I visited Onsu with a friend after seeing it on Instagram, and it certainly looks as stylish as it does online. The décor is modern and well presented, which is what attracted us in the first place. The only downside to the space is that it's quite small, and the tables are very close together, making it feel a little cramped.

The service was friendly and welcoming, and the staff recommended some drinks that turned out to be excellent. The pistachio and coconut iced drink was incredibly refreshing, and the famous dirty iced coffee definitely lived up to its reputation.

Unfortunately, the food didn't match the quality of the drinks. Although the desserts looked beautiful and were very Instagram-worthy, they lacked flavour and were  disappointing. We also ordered the tikka chicken masala, which was so spicy that it was almost impossible to eat, even for someone who normally enjoys spicy food. The heat completely overpowered the other flavours.

Overall, Onsu is a lovely café for its atmosphere and outstanding drinks, but based on our experience, the food didn't live up to the expectations. I'd happily return for the iced drinks, but I'd probably skip the food next time.

text.text:
If you love cookies and ice cream, then Crème is definitely worth visiting. The cookies here are genuinely some of the best I’ve had in London. They’re thick, soft in the centre, slightly crisp on the outside, and served warm.

The milk chocolate cookie is clearly the bestseller for a reason, but they also have great flavours like white chocolate miso, banana dark chocolate, vegan double chocolate, and dark chocolate.

The soft serve ice cream portions are generous and actually worth the price, which is becoming rare in London dessert spots. Combining the cookies with the ice cream is probably the best way to enjoy it.

The shop itself has a cool Soho dessert spot feel to it. Small, busy, and clearly popular. Definitely somewhere worth trying if you want a proper dessert stop rather than just another average cookie place.

We came to Cutter & Squidge for their themed Miffy afternoon tea, which was £45 for 90 minutes.

Overall, it was a nice experience, and the food was delicious. However they are quite cheeky with drinks - staff failed to explain that you are either allowed to have one single coffee for the entire 90 minutes, OR unlimited teas. We were told both standard teas and coffee were included but you could only have one coffee, whereas tea was unlimited. For £45 it is quite tight to not let us also have a single cup of tea after a latte - unlimited tea is the standard at afternoon tea, and this one is premium priced, so quite disappointing that if you’ve dared to have a single latte this isn’t available. It’s just a teabag in a pot it hardly costs the business a penny. Also worth noting the Miffy themed drinks or anything beyond standard tea & coffee isn’t included, for children who may be dissatisfied with this. They don’t cater to dietary restrictions either so keep that in mind and check the offering beforehand.

The place is beautifully decorated and otherwise really worth a stop, just don’t get caught out like us!

First, we tried the leche flan danish. It was basically a regular Danish pastry topped with leche flan. It was good, but the flan tasted more like custard than the traditional leche flan I was expecting. The corned beef hash sando was unfortunately a bit too salty, although the portion was generous enough to share. I was also really excited to try the ube matcha, but it tasted more like an ube latte with little to no matcha flavour at all.

Given the price range, I wish they had more seating so we could enjoy our food there. Since it gets pretty busy, the wait was a bit longer than we expected. Overall, I’m still glad we gave it a try, but it didn’t quite live up to the hype for me.

We stopped by Chinatown Bakery while exploring London's Chinatown. Everything looked so good, but we were already quite full, so we decided to try just one thing, the mini fish-shaped cakes filled with custard.

They were absolutely delicious! The custard filling wasn't overly sweet, just the perfect amount, and the cakes were incredibly soft. They're made fresh right in front of you, so you always get a hot batch. In fact, my mum got a little too excited and burned her mouth because they were so fresh, so definitely give them a minute to cool down before taking a bite!

We got four mini custard fish for £3.20, which I think is a very reasonable price for a freshly made snack. I'd happily buy them again.

The person at the fish stand was kind, welcoming, and helpful. There was no queue when we visited, so we were served very quickly. The bakery itself was clean, well organised, smelled amazing, and had a huge variety of baked goods to choose from. It is quite small inside, though, and because it's so popular it gets very crowded, making it a little difficult to move around and browse everything comfortably.

Next time I'm in London, I'll definitely be back to try more of their baked goods. If you're visiting Chinatown, I'd definitely recommend stopping by!

If you are looking for authentic Japanese matcha, this is the place. Unlike many coffee shops that use sweetened powders, Tsujiri offers a deep, earthy, and high quality matcha that isn't overpowered by sugar.

I tried the Tsujiri Sundae with red bean and mochi, and the balance of textures was spot on. The soft serve is smooth and has that distinct, slightly bitter tea flavor that proves its quality. The roasted rice toppings add a great crunch, and the warabimochi is a must try for a more traditional experience.

It’s a small, busy spot, but it’s perfect for a quick, sophisticated treat while walking through the city.

So I saw a recommendation for Auntea Jenny by a YouTuber who I follow and she had an iced lemon and lime fruit tea, which is one of my favourites. So I decided to try it. I would recommend and go again ❤️

Such a lovely bubble tea spot in Soho! The location on Frith Street is super convenient, making it the perfect place to stop for a drink while exploring or shopping around Soho.

I ordered the Brown Sugar Bubble Fresh Milk, and it was absolutely delicious. One of the best things about this place is that you can actually watch the staff prepare the drink right in front of you. Seeing them stir-fry the brown sugar together with the tapioca pearls and then add fresh milk makes the whole experience feel extra special — and the amazing smell of caramelised brown sugar fills the air!

The pearls were freshly made, perfectly chewy and coated in a rich, fragrant brown sugar syrup. Combined with fresh cold milk, the drink wasn’t overly sweet and had a really nice balance of creamy and caramel flavours.

The shop also has that cosy, familiar Taiwanese bubble tea shop atmosphere, making it a great place to sit down and chat with friends or simply grab a drink to enjoy while walking around Soho.

Definitely worth a visit if you’re a bubble tea lover!

I have passed this place many times and been put off by the huge queues.

On a bank holiday, I took the chance to try it as it seemed quiet. However it turned out to be quite stressful on a hot sunny day.
As soon as you walk inside there is a till but no one was there to seve.
The kitchen looked busy and full of staff.
Then as you look to your left that is the rest of the shop, a small area to wait/collect your drink, which has the shop glass front on one side and the counter and kitchen the other. As it was a hot day, it was hot inside and then people came in to wait and collect the drinks.

There are qr codes for you to download the app to order your drinks. This really isn't great when the network  keeps dropping though.

Whilst at checkout on the app I noticed my order was rounded up and I couldnt figure out why, so I left it.
Much later I found out I was charged 20p for a paper bag which I did not need or want.

The app is good to let you know where it is in the queue and to let u know when it is waiting to be collected.
I don't believe they called out my name or number, therefore I had to collect it myself, waving down a staff member.  She was friendly and gave me my drinks.

The mangoes inside the drinks were stringy, I had to spit these out. They were not made with care.
The cups are nice and solid but seems wasteful.
It was also probably the most expensive teas we have had

Overall for us, we did not enjoy the experience of ordering and the carelessness with the mangoes, it was not worth it.

Tried three items at Milksha and honestly all of them were solid.

The Brown Sugar Matcha Milk with Honey Pearls was my favourite. The matcha flavour was rich but not bitter, and the brown sugar added a nice caramel depth without being overly sweet. The honey pearls were soft and slightly chewy, not too heavy like some tapioca pearls can be.

The Strawberry Matcha was more refreshing. You get that fruity acidity from the strawberry at the bottom, which balances out the creaminess of the milk and matcha on top. It’s lighter and easier to drink if you don’t want something too sweet.

Also tried the Taro Dessert with Taro Balls and Sago. This was surprisingly good. The taro chunks tasted very natural, not artificial at all, and the taro balls had a nice chewy texture. The sago added a bit of softness and made the whole dessert feel quite comforting.

Overall, good quality drinks and desserts. Not overly sweet, which I really appreciate. Would definitely come back.

I’ve been a customer of Kissaten since it first opened inside the laundromat. Over the years, I’ve watched it grow in popularity, but unfortunately, the quality of service has declined. Today was the first time I left genuinely frustrated.

The shop is now overcrowded with gacha machines, leaving very little space to stand or move comfortably. A single small service window now handles both gacha and drink orders, resulting in long delays—especially when someone places a large gacha order. During my visit, around ten drink orders appeared to be stalled with no visible progress. Several customers voiced their concerns, but the staff seemed largely indifferent.

After waiting for about 15 minutes, we were informed that our drink was unavailable—something that should have been communicated at the time of ordering. No apology or compensation was offered. When we asked for a refund and expressed our frustration, the staff member told us we were “holding her up.” We weren’t given any proof of refund, only a verbal confirmation.

It’s disappointing to see a place I once really enjoyed become so poorly managed. What used to feel welcoming and efficient now feels disorganised and dismissive toward customers.

As for the gachapon machines, they feel questionable at best. My sister visited a few months ago and received the exact same keychain twice in a row—of the least popular character. Recently, I spent £6 on a broken Sanrio toy that didn’t even light up as advertised. It’s hard not to feel that the odds or quality aren’t quite as they should be.

The boba itself is decent but nothing special—certainly not enough to justify the experience or the prices.

Overall, Kissaten remains a cute and aesthetic stop in Soho, but at this point, it’s more style than substance. Sadly, it’s no longer worth the money or the frustration.

Diners like this cafe's delicious cakes, especially the matcha and crepe varieties, which are often described as not too sweet and authentic. They also highlight the friendly staff and the cafe's late closing hours, making it ideal for evening hangouts.

Some reviews mention the drinks can be overpriced.
